title: How I used Generative AI to develop my commercial game,  Rats Survivors
author: Elegant_Kick5667
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I wanted to share a little bit about the development process behind my upcoming commercial game, **Rats Survivors**, and be completely transparent about how generative AI has been used throughout development.

🐔 **Rats Survivors** is a roguelike survival game inspired by games like *Vampire Survivors*, but with its own characters, mechanics, progression systems, and world. The game is being developed by my studio, **Forge Games**.

🤖 **How I use AI during development:**

* **Programming & debugging:** I use AI coding assistants such as **ChatGPT, Gemini, and other coding models** to help prototype systems, investigate bugs, refactor code, and implement gameplay mechanics. I still review, test, and adapt the generated code to fit the game's architecture.
* **Game design:** AI has also been useful as a brainstorming and iteration tool. I've used it to explore ideas for skills, enemy behaviors, progression, synergies, balancing, and gameplay systems. The final decisions are made based on how the mechanics actually feel in the game.
* **Visual development:** AI tools have been used during the creation and exploration of some visual assets and concepts. I use them as part of the development workflow alongside traditional tools and manually created/edited assets.
* **Narrative & world building:** I've also used AI to brainstorm ideas for the game's lore, characters, names, descriptions, and other pieces of game content.

For me, AI isn't replacing the development process — it's another tool in the toolbox. I still have to decide what belongs in the game, implement it, test it, iterate on it, and make sure everything works together.

I'm sharing this because I think it's important to be transparent about AI usage in game development, especially for a commercial project.

If you're also developing a game with AI-assisted tools, I'd love to hear how you're using them in your workflow. What has actually been useful for you, and what hasn't?
